definition: NetOwl is a suite of multilingual text and identity analytics products that analyze big data in the form of text data – reports, web, social media, etc.
details: – as well as structured entity data about people, organizations, places, and things. NetOwl utilizes artificial intelligence (AI)-based approaches, including natural language processing (NLP), machine learning (ML), and computational linguistics, to extract entities, relationships, and events; to perform sentiment analysis; to assign latitude/longitude to geographical references in text; to translate names written in foreign languages; and to perform name matching and identity resolution. NetOwl's uses include semantic search and discovery, geospatial analysis, intelligence analysis, content enrichment, compliance monitoring, cyber threat monitoring, risk management, and bioinformatics.

explainer.lead: NetOwl is a suite of multilingual text and identity analytics products that analyze big data in the form of text, such as reports, web and social media, plus structured entity data about people, organizations, places and things.

tiers.eli5: It reads huge piles of text in many languages and picks out the who, what, where and how people feel about it.
tiers.practitioner: It uses NLP, machine learning and computational linguistics to extract entities, relationships and events, run sentiment analysis, assign latitude/longitude to place references, translate foreign names, and match names for identity resolution. A pitfall is that identity resolution across languages and name variants is where such pipelines are hardest.
tiers.paperLevel: AI-based text and identity analytics drawing on natural language processing, machine learning and computational linguistics, over text and structured entity data.

explainer.example: A news feed mentioning a place and a person is processed to extract the entities and event, score sentiment, and attach coordinates to the place.
